official.deadline_note: Two later supporting deadlines beat the November 15 cut-off in practice: UBC requires any documents needed to evaluate your UBC application and proof that you meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard by January 31, 2027, which is NOT the date printed in your 'Your UBC Application - Next Steps' email and is earlier than the general ELAS document deadline of February 15. The general UBC application deadline is January 15, 2027 and the first-year housing application deadline is May 1, 2027.
official.application_cycle: September 2027 intake (Winter Session, September 2027 to April 2028); application opened October 5, 2026 and closes November 15, 2026.
official.status_note: The International Scholars page states 'Applications for the September 2027 are open.' UBC's application portal lists an opening date of October 5, 2026 (09:00 PDT) and a deadline of November 15, 2026 (11:59 PM PST), and the dates and deadlines page confirms November 15, 2026 (11:59 p.m. PST) as the deadline for international applicants to apply to UBC and submit an award application for the UBC International Scholars Program awards.
official.tuition_coverage_note: UBC publishes no per-award dollar figure. For the Vantage One Excellence Award, UBC Vantage College states awards 'ranging in value up to the full cost of the student's academic program and living costs', with 'the value of each award... dependent on the recipient's financial need'. For the programme as a whole, the International Scholars page states the financial need estimate is 'the amount that represents how much financial support you would require to live and study at UBC after all your resources have been accounted for'.
benefits: Financial support determined by assessed financial need - 'the amount that represents how much financial support you would require to live and study at UBC after all your resources have been accounted for'

For the Vantage One Excellence Award, awards 'ranging in value up to the full cost of the student's academic program and living costs', renewable for up to three additional years or to degree completion, whichever is less, provided the recipient maintains their status as an international student in Canada, with the award reviewed annually for academic progress and financial need
A globally recognized degree at a top university, studying with the brightest students in the world
Unique learning opportunities, with the option to participate in exchange and co-op
Dedicated advising and support from International Scholars Program advisors, plus skill building workshops and retreats
Membership of a cohort drawn from 111+ countries; UBC reports 680+ International Scholars since 2001 and 200+ hours of developmental workshops and one-on-one support over the course of a degree
eligibility: You are an international student who will be studying in Canada on a Canadian study permit.

You are entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school, and you are applying for your first undergraduate degree. Applicants for 2027 Winter session must have graduated from high school no earlier than June 2026.
You demonstrate superior academic achievement (achieve all As or equivalent standard) and meet UBC's admission requirements, including general and degree-specific requirements.

You can prove a significant level of financial need: it would be impossible for you to pursue a UBC degree without meaningful financial help, and your family is not able to afford a significant level of your educational costs and does not have access to external funding.
You meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard, or the English language requirement for UBC Vantage College if applying through Vantage One.
You are nominated by your high school or a qualifying registered non-profit organization, and you provide a reference from an academic referee who is a different person from your nominator.
requirements: Submit your UBC Admissions application first - the award application requests confirmation of UBC application submission and cannot be completed until the admissions application is done.
Secure one nominator (guidance counsellor, principal, administrator, etc.) and one teacher referee; they must be two different people.

A high school or registered non-profit organization may nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver (including Vantage College) and one student for UBC Okanagan; a non-profit qualifies where it acts as an educational institution in place of a high school, or offers an educational, leadership development and mentorship program to high school graduates from less fortunate backgrounds, and UBC says this option is typically reserved for applicants from war-torn, politically unstable, or economically disadvantaged areas.

Complete the in-depth financial sections: annual income and expenses, family wealth and assets, dependents and annual school fees, and sources of financial support, using UBC's cost estimator to calculate family contributions and financial need.
Complete 4 essay questions of approximately 150-250 words each, and complete a video interview if invited (one week to record responses on the online application platform).

The nominator and teacher referee forms must be completed and submitted a few days before November 15; you cannot complete your award application until both have been submitted. UBC states there are no exceptions to the eligibility criteria.
documents: Official documents that demonstrate your financial need, including documents outlining your family's gross income, expenses and family assets (reviewed as part of UBC's financial assessment)
Transcripts and high school academic certificates required to evaluate your UBC application, submitted by January 31
Official English language test results, if an English language test is required, received by UBC Admissions by January 31
The nominator's completed and submitted nomination form
The teacher referee's completed and submitted reference form
4 written essay responses of approximately 150-250 words each, entered in the award application
selection_criteria: Demonstrated leadership qualities, exceptional contributions to their communities, and outstanding academic performance, with superior academic achievement at the all-As or equivalent standard
Assessed significant financial need, established by reviewing documents outlining the family's gross income, expenses and family assets
Applicants may be invited to a video interview to share more about themselves and reflect on past educational and leadership experiences beyond the written application
You will not select which award you wish to receive - UBC's team automatically considers you for the awards you are eligible for

If you apply to the International Scholars Program you will not be considered for merit-based awards, including International Major Entrance Scholarships and Outstanding International Student Awards; applicants may only be considered for either UBC's merit-based or its financial need-based award program
coverage: Financial support determined by assessed financial need, described as the amount representing how much support you would require to live and study at UBC after all your resources have been accounted for
For the Vantage One Excellence Award only, value stated as ranging up to the full cost of a student's academic program and living expenses
Dedicated advising and support from International Scholars Program advisors
application_method: Decide on your academic program and campus (you are considered for your first choice program, but you should still select a second choice program), then discuss the nomination with your school and confirm your high school or registered non-profit is able to nominate you and that you meet the eligibility requirements.
Submit your UBC Admissions application - this is required before your award application can be started.
Create your award application account, email your nominator and teacher referee requesting their recommendations, and invite them to complete their forms in the portal.
Gather your family and financial information, complete your sections of the award application, and the 4 essays.

Have the nominator and teacher referee complete and submit their forms a few days before November 15, then submit your completed award application by November 15, and clear the January 31 gate for admission documents and English language results.
Complete the video interview if invited (one week to record responses), and check your email including spam filters for updates.
official.application_route: Apply to UBC first, then create an account on UBC's undergraduate scholarship application portal and submit the International Scholars Program application, inviting your nominator and teacher referee to complete their forms there.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to international students of any nationality who will be studying in Canada on a Canadian study permit; no country-of-residence restriction is published, and UBC reports 111+ countries represented among International Scholars.
official.international_eligibility: International students only - eligibility requires that you are an international student who will be studying in Canada on a Canadian study permit, entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Nomination is required: one nominator (guidance counsellor, principal, administrator, etc.) from your high school or a qualifying registered non-profit, plus one teacher referee who must be a different person. A high school or registered non-profit may nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver (including Vantage College) and one student for UBC Okanagan. These degrees are explicitly not eligible: Bachelor of Nursing (Okanagan and Vancouver), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management degree, dual degrees, joint degrees between UBC Okanagan and UBC Vancouver, and joint degrees with other post-secondary institutions.
official.description: UBC describes the International Scholars Program as being for international students who have demonstrated leadership qualities, exceptional contributions to their communities, have outstanding academic performance, and require meaningful financial support to attend UBC, bringing together Scholars from diverse countries and cultures to foster a globally connected learning community. There are four categories of need-and-merit-based awards available through the programme, and applicants do not select which award they receive - UBC's team automatically considers each applicant for the awards they are eligible for.
official.region: North America (Canada - UBC Vancouver and UBC Okanagan)
official.program_type: University scholarship - need-and-merit based entrance award programme for international undergraduate students
official.english_requirement: You must meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard by January 31; if you do not satisfy this for direct entry you may be eligible for UBC Vantage College and the Vantage One Excellence Award, which requires the English language requirement for UBC Vantage College. If you are required to take an English language test, you must complete it early enough for UBC Admissions to receive your official test results by January 31. UBC's English Language Admission Standard minimums are IELTS Academic 6.5 with no part below 6.0, TOEFL iBT overall 90 (Reading 22, Listening 22, Writing 21, Speaking 21), PTE 65, CAEL 70, Cambridge B2 First/C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 180, or Duolingo English Test 125, with test scores from January 1, 2025 onwards. UBC Vantage College's requirement is IELTS 5.5 with 5.0 in speaking and listening and 5.5 in reading and writing, TOEFL iBT 70 with no section below 16, Duolingo 105-124, CAEL 50, or completion of Level 400 of the UBC English Language Institute's English for Academic Purposes program.

verification.notes: Checked the International Scholars programme page, the live 2027 application portal on UBC's scholarship site, the dates and deadlines page, the UBC Vantage College awards page, and UBC's English language competency page; no official UBC page publishes a dollar value for these need-based awards, so the amount, currency and period are left null.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a nomination-gated, need-and-merit programme spread across four separate awards, and you apply once through UBC's scholarship portal without choosing an award name - UBC's committee decides which of the Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow, Donald A. Wehrung, International Impact, or Vantage One Excellence awards you are considered for. Because the award is calculated backwards from your assessed financial need rather than from a fixed stipend, two applicants with identical grades can receive very different values, so your documented need is as decisive as your transcript. Applying here is a deliberate either/or choice: it removes you from consideration for UBC's merit-based International Major Entrance Scholarship and Outstanding International Student Award, and there are no exceptions to the eligibility criteria.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent international secondary-school graduates with an all-A record, provable and documented high financial need, and a school or qualifying non-profit willing to nominate them.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm in writing that your school or non-profit has a nomination slot free for your campus: a school or non-profit may nominate only two students for UBC Vancouver (including Vantage College) and one for UBC Okanagan.

If you are relying on a non-profit nominator, verify it genuinely acts as an educational institution in place of a high school or runs an educational, leadership development and mentorship programme for disadvantaged graduates - UBC says this route is typically reserved for applicants from war-torn, politically unstable or economically disadvantaged areas.
Submit your UBC admissions application early: the award application asks you to confirm you have applied to UBC and you cannot open the award form until that is done.
Book any English test so official results physically reach UBC Admissions by January 31, 2027, not merely your test date - and check your test score validity is on or after January 1, 2025.
Collect official family income, expense, asset and dependents' fee documents before you start, and run UBC's cost estimator so your stated need matches the evidence you attach.
Have your nominator and teacher referee submit their forms several days before November 15 so your own application is not left in a permanently incomplete state.
common_rejection_risks: No nomination, or a school that has already used its two Vancouver slots or its single Okanagan slot.
Naming the same person as nominator and teacher referee - UBC requires two different people, and it is a hard eligibility rule.
Being eliminated at the financial assessment because family income and assets leave insufficient assessed need, even with a perfect transcript.

Choosing an excluded degree - Nursing, Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management, dual degrees, and joint degrees with other institutions are explicitly not eligible.
Missing all-As or equivalent, or not meeting UBC's general and degree-specific admission requirements.
Missing the January 31, 2027 document and English-language deadline, which UBC enforces instead of the date in your 'next steps' email; a single A below the all-As standard.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond your assessed need: flights to Canada, study permit and biometrics fees, a residence deposit or off-campus rent and living costs above UBC's cost-estimator figure, and incidental first-year costs. UBC's cost estimator is the reference point for the baseline you are expected to fund yourself.
document_audit: Financial need must be evidenced by official documents - gross income, expenses and family assets - not by figures you type into the form alone.
Transcripts and high school certificates go to UBC's Undergraduate Admissions Office by January 31 for ISP applicants, overriding the date in the 'Your UBC Application - Next Steps' email.
English proficiency must be proven with official scores received by UBC by January 31; booked or pending results do not count, and scores must be from January 1, 2025 onwards.
The teacher referee should be someone familiar with your work in your chosen area of study - a referee who cannot speak to the subject weakens the file.
Four essays of roughly 150-250 words each must be written into the portal, so drafting them offline is far safer than composing them inside the form.
Still select a second-choice program even though award consideration is based on your first choice.
alerts: The portal opens October 5, 2026 (09:00 PDT) and closes November 15, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. PST - UBC warns that applications started shortly before the deadline are less likely to succeed.

January 31, 2027 is the real cut-off for supporting admission documents and proof of the English Language Admission Standard; UBC cannot proceed with your ISP application if anything needed for admission is missing.

Applying to this programme forfeits consideration for merit-based awards, including International Major Entrance Scholarships and Outstanding International Student Awards - you cannot hold both routes.
Do not apply for residence until award decisions are released: the first-year housing application deadline is May 1, 2027.
Results come out on a rolling basis February to April 2027 and are confirmed by early- to mid-April, so keep monitoring email and mark all UBC addresses as safe.
The Vantage One Excellence Award is reviewed annually for academic progress and financial need, so renewal is not automatic even after you win.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to UBC, open the UBC scholarship portal, invite your nominator and teacher referee, complete the financial sections and four essays, wait for both external forms to land, then submit by November 15 and clear the January 31 documents and English-test gate.
